What makes industrial & engineering manufacturers different

  • RFQs with drawings and BOQs wait in inboxes while one or two estimators rebuild a costing sheet for each enquiry.

  • OEM customers expect 8D reports and CAPA evidence, but NCR records sit on paper, in email and in photo galleries.

  • Downtime reasons and shift output are recorded inconsistently, so OEE discussions turn into debates about the numbers.

  • Warranty, AMC and spare-part requests depend on coordinators searching spreadsheets for serial numbers and contract dates.

Where automation helps industrial & engineering manufacturers

  • Drawing-based quote drafts

    Extract material, dimensions, tolerances, finish and quantity breaks from RFQs and drawings, match them to past quotes and current rates, and hand the estimator a costing draft to correct and approve.

  • Marketplace and website enquiry routing

    Route IndiaMART, TradeIndia and website enquiries by product family and territory, with missing technical details listed as questions for the rep's first call.

  • 8D-ready NCR and complaint handling

    Capture defects with drawing revision, heat or lot number and photos at inspection, track containment and CAPA actions, and compile 8D drafts for QA to finalize.

  • Line and shift performance dashboard

    Combine ERP production entries, MES exports and shift sheets into availability, performance and quality views, using downtime reasons that supervisors have confirmed.

  • Maintenance and statutory inspection reminders

    Generate PM work orders from run hours or dates, log breakdowns with cause and spares, and remind the safety team of inspections due for lifting equipment and pressure vessels.

  • Installed-base service desk

    Check serial numbers against warranty and AMC terms, give engineers manual-based checks before the visit, and turn spare-part needs into stock checks or quotes.

Enquiry & qualificationStandard3–5 weeks

Marketplace and website enquiry capture with routing

Pull every enquiry from IndiaMART, TradeIndia, the website and the RFQ inbox into one CRM queue, remove duplicates, extract what the buyer needs and route it to the right product or territory owner with a response deadline.

Industrial & engineering manufacturers · Process, chemical & pharma manufacturing · Contract & private-label manufacturing

Open the automation blueprint

The problem

Enquiries arrive through marketplace dashboards, email, website forms, phone calls and trade-fair cards. Sales coordinators copy them by hand, duplicates from the same buyer go to two reps, and enquiries that arrive after hours wait until someone notices them. Buyers who send the same RFQ to several suppliers often shortlist whoever replies first with a sensible question.

Trigger

A new lead appears through the IndiaMART Lead Manager API, a marketplace or website form notification arrives, or an email lands in the shared RFQ inbox.

How it runs

  1. Collect leads from the IndiaMART Lead Manager API, other marketplace notifications, website forms and the RFQ mailbox into one queue.
  2. Normalize names, phone numbers, company names and GSTIN where given, then match against existing CRM accounts and open enquiries to avoid duplicate follow-up.
  3. Use an AI model to extract product, grade or specification, quantity, delivery location, required date and attachments, and list missing information as questions for the rep.
  4. Score fit against agreed rules such as product range, minimum order, serviceable region and buyer type, and route to the product or territory owner with a response deadline.
  5. Send an acknowledgement by email, or by WhatsApp only where the buyer started the chat or opted in, and alert the owner in Slack or the CRM app.
  6. Escalate enquiries with no human response by the deadline to the sales coordinator.

Human checkpoint

The sales coordinator reviews low-confidence extractions, out-of-territory enquiries and anything flagged as a large or strategic account before routing. Reps qualify every enquiry by call or email; the automation never sends prices or delivery commitments.

Systems it connects

  • TradeIndia and other B2B marketplaces
  • Website forms and RFQ mailbox

Data & consent

Only fields needed for qualification are kept in the CRM; raw marketplace payloads are held for a short agreed period for troubleshooting, then deleted. Promotional messages go only to contacts who agreed to receive them. Access follows CRM roles.

What we deliver

  • Unified enquiry queue in the CRM
  • Extraction and routing rules with confidence thresholds
  • Response-time and source dashboard
  • Escalation alerts for unowned enquiries

How we measure it

  • Enquiry first-response time
  • Duplicate enquiry rate
  • Enquiries without an owner after the deadline
  • Qualified enquiries by source

Specification, samples & quoteAdvanced6–10 weeks

RFQ-to-quote drafting with estimator approval

Turn RFQ emails, drawings and BOQs into a structured costing draft based on your item master, past quotes and current rates, so the estimator reviews and approves a quote instead of building it from scratch, and the eventual PO is checked against it.

Industrial & engineering manufacturers · Contract & private-label manufacturing

Open the automation blueprint

The problem

Quoting depends on one or two experienced estimators who rebuild costing sheets in Excel for every RFQ, look up old quotes from memory and chase purchase for current material rates. Turnaround slips when they are on the shop floor or traveling, assumptions are not recorded, and the same part can be priced differently for different buyers.

Trigger

An enquiry is marked qualified in the CRM with an RFQ, drawing, specification sheet, formulation brief or BOQ attached.

How it runs

  1. Extract line items, material grade, quantity breaks, finish, packing and delivery terms from the RFQ, BOQ and drawing title blocks and notes, flagging any dimension or tolerance it cannot read with confidence.
  2. Match each line to the item master, released drawing revisions where the PDM exposes an API or export, and similar past quotes, and show what changed since the last quote to this buyer.
  3. Pull current raw material rates, machine-hour or conversion rates, tooling and freight assumptions from the rate tables maintained by purchase and costing.
  4. Generate a costing sheet and quote draft in the standard template, with assumptions, deviations from the buyer's specification and open technical questions listed.
  5. Route the draft to the estimator in a review screen; discounts beyond the agreed matrix go to the sales head for approval.
  6. Send the approved quote as a PDF from the rep's address, log the version in the CRM, schedule follow-ups and capture win or loss reasons at close.
  7. When the buyer's PO arrives, compare price, quantity, delivery and terms with the approved quote and stage a draft sales order for the commercial manager.

Human checkpoint

The estimator or applications engineer checks every technical interpretation, cost element and price before release, and the sales head approves discounts outside the matrix. Nothing reaches a buyer without a named approver recorded against that quote version.

Systems it connects

  • ERP item master and price lists
  • Costing sheets and rate tables
  • CAD/PDM drawing repository

Data & consent

Uses buyer RFQs and drawings, which may be confidential or under NDA, plus internal costs and margins. Documents are processed under API terms that exclude training on client data, in a region the client approves where the provider offers one, with access limited to sales, estimation and management. Margin fields are hidden from roles that do not need them, and files follow the client's document retention policy.

What we deliver

  • Structured RFQ extraction with confidence flags
  • Costing draft and quote generator in the standard template
  • Estimator review and approval screen
  • Quote register with versions, approvals and win or loss reasons
  • PO-to-quote comparison with draft sales order

How we measure it

  • Quote turnaround time
  • Quote-to-order conversion
  • Quotes revised after buyer queries
  • Estimator time per quote

Plan, procure, make & checkStandard4–6 weeks

Daily production and OEE-style reporting from ERP and MES data

Collect shift production, downtime and rejection entries from the ERP, MES or shift sheets, check them for gaps, and publish a plant dashboard and a short written summary in time for the morning production meeting.

Industrial & engineering manufacturers · Process, chemical & pharma manufacturing

Open the automation blueprint

The problem

Production figures arrive from different lines as Excel sheets, WhatsApp photos of logbooks and ERP entries made a day late. The morning meeting spends its time agreeing numbers instead of acting on them, downtime reasons are recorded inconsistently, and lines or shifts cannot be compared reliably.

Trigger

A scheduled run after each shift or at a fixed time before the morning meeting, reading the latest ERP, MES or shift sheet data.

How it runs

  1. Pull shift output, planned and actual run time, downtime with reason codes, rejections and rework from ERP, MES exports or structured shift sheets.
  2. Flag missing shifts, impossible values and unmapped downtime reasons to the line supervisor before the report runs.
  3. Model the data in a warehouse with agreed definitions and calculate availability, performance and quality where machine and standard-rate data allow; for batch plants, report yield and cycle time per batch.
  4. Publish a Power BI dashboard by plant, line, shift and product, with trends and the top downtime reasons.
  5. Draft a short written summary of the main variances for the plant head, linked to the underlying numbers.

Human checkpoint

Line supervisors confirm reason codes and corrections before figures are published, and the plant head reviews the written summary and owns any action. For GxP plants the dashboard is a reporting copy; batch records in validated systems remain the record.

Plan, procure, make & checkStandard4–6 weeks

Quality NCR, customer complaint and CAPA routing

Raise non-conformances and customer complaints with photos, lot and part details, route them to the right quality owner, track containment and CAPA actions to closure, and draft 8D reports for QA approval.

Industrial & engineering manufacturers · Contract & private-label manufacturing

Open the automation blueprint

The problem

NCRs are raised on paper or by email, containment depends on who remembers, and CAPA due dates slip between shifts. OEM customers and brand owners expect 8D reports and evidence of effectiveness checks, but the quality team spends days compiling them from scattered photos, test results and email threads.

Trigger

An inspector logs a non-conformance at incoming, in-process or final inspection, or a customer complaint arrives by email, portal or through the account manager.

How it runs

  1. Capture the NCR with part or product, drawing revision, batch or lot, quantity, defect type and photos through a mobile form.
  2. Assign a number, route it to the QA owner for that product line and open containment tasks with due dates.
  3. Show similar past NCRs and their root causes, and draft a structured 5-why or 8D outline from the record for the quality engineer to complete.
  4. Track corrective and preventive actions, send reminders before due dates and schedule effectiveness checks.
  5. Compile the customer-facing 8D or complaint response from approved content for QA sign-off.

Human checkpoint

The QA manager decides disposition (use as is, rework, scrap or return) and approves root cause, CAPA closure and every customer-facing report. AI output is marked as draft and never closes a record. On GxP sites, deviations and CAPAs stay in the validated QMS.

Plan, procure, make & checkStandard4–6 weeks

Preventive maintenance alerts and breakdown logging

Generate maintenance work orders from calendar, run-hour or count schedules, remind technicians and supervisors before due dates, log breakdowns with cause and spares used, and track statutory inspection dates.

Industrial & engineering manufacturers · Process, chemical & pharma manufacturing

Open the automation blueprint

The problem

Preventive maintenance schedules sit in Excel or in a CMMS nobody updates. Tasks are skipped under production pressure, breakdowns are fixed without recording cause or parts, and due dates for statutory inspections of lifting equipment and pressure vessels live in one person's diary.

Trigger

A schedule threshold is reached by date, run hours or production count from MES or meter readings, or an operator reports a breakdown.

How it runs

  1. Set up the asset register with maintenance plans, checklists and statutory inspection due dates agreed with the maintenance head.
  2. Create work orders ahead of the due date and notify the assigned technician and supervisor, escalating tasks that become overdue.
  3. Let technicians close work orders on mobile with checklist results, readings, photos and spares used.
  4. Log breakdowns with symptom, cause, downtime and parts, and feed them into MTBF and MTTR reporting.
  5. Remind the safety officer and the occupier's team of upcoming statutory inspections and the reports due from competent persons.

Human checkpoint

The maintenance head approves schedule changes and every deferral, and safety-critical tasks cannot be deferred without a named sign-off. For GxP equipment, calibration and maintenance records stay in the validated CMMS or logbook; this workflow only sends reminders.

Service, field visits & reorderAdvanced6–8 weeks

Service, AMC and warranty tickets with spare-part requests

Log service requests with machine serial number, photos and symptoms, check warranty or AMC status, assign the right engineer, suggest checks from approved manuals and turn spare-part needs into stock checks or quotes.

Industrial & engineering manufacturers · Distributors & dealer networks

Open the automation blueprint

The problem

Customers and dealers report breakdowns by calling whoever they know. Service coordinators look up warranty and AMC status in spreadsheets, engineers travel without the right spare or manual, and parts quotes for out-of-warranty machines take days. AMC renewals lapse because nobody tracks expiry dates.

Trigger

A customer or dealer raises a request on WhatsApp, the portal or by email, or an AMC visit or renewal date comes due.

How it runs

  1. Capture the machine serial number, site, symptoms, error codes and photos through a guided WhatsApp or portal form.
  2. Check the serial number against the installed base, warranty terms and AMC contract, and show the machine's service history.
  3. Suggest likely causes and checks for the engineer from approved manuals and past tickets, with links to the source pages.
  4. Assign an engineer by territory, skill and availability, start SLA timers and update the customer with approved templates.
  5. For parts, check stock and raise a warranty replacement request or an out-of-warranty quote for approval; remind customers of AMC renewals and preventive visits.
  6. Close the ticket with the engineer's report, parts used and customer sign-off.

Human checkpoint

The service engineer diagnoses and decides the repair, and the service manager approves warranty acceptance or rejection and any goodwill. Faults involving guarding, interlocks, pressure or electrical hazards go straight to an engineer; the assistant never advises bypassing a safety device.
